words.definition: differences in characteristics among individuals of the same species
words.example: Genetic and environmental factors both contribute to variation within a population.

words.definition: a group of organisms that share defining characteristics and can be distinguished from other such groups
words.example: A species is a fundamental unit used to describe biological diversity.

words.definition: a way of defining species by differences in observable structural characteristics
words.example: The morphological species concept is useful when reproductive data are unavailable.

words.definition: the system of naming each species with a two-part scientific name consisting of genus and specific epithet
words.example: In binomial nomenclature, Homo sapiens is the scientific name for humans.

words.definition: a taxonomic group containing one or more closely related species
words.example: The genus Homo includes humans and several extinct relatives.

words.definition: the concept that a species consists of populations that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring
words.example: The biological species concept emphasizes reproductive compatibility.

words.definition: offspring capable of reproducing and producing the next generation
words.example: Members of the same biological species can usually produce fertile offspring.

words.definition: the accumulation of differences between populations over time
words.example: Population divergence can increase when gene flow is reduced.

words.definition: the biological or practical distinction separating one species from another
words.example: Hybridization can make a species boundary difficult to define.

words.definition: the number of chromosomes present in a cell or species-specific chromosome set
words.example: Humans have 46 chromosomes in most somatic cells.

words.definition: the number and appearance of chromosomes characteristic of an individual or species
words.example: A human karyotype normally contains 23 chromosome pairs.

words.definition: an ordered image of chromosomes arranged in homologous pairs
words.example: A karyogram can reveal abnormalities in chromosome number.

words.definition: the chromosome region where sister chromatids are joined and spindle attachment occurs during division
words.example: The centromere is visible as a constricted region on a condensed chromosome.

words.definition: the complete genetic material of an organism or cell
words.example: The human genome contains all of the DNA in a human cell.

words.definition: the total amount of DNA in one complete genome
words.example: Genome size varies greatly among species.

words.definition: differences in DNA sequence or genome structure among individuals or populations
words.example: Genomic variation provides evidence about relatedness among populations.

words.definition: determining the nucleotide sequence of nearly all DNA in an organism's genome
words.japanese: 全ゲノムシーケンシング
words.example: Whole-genome sequencing can reveal genetic differences among individuals.
